title: Bishop's Opening: the ideas
line: The bishop comes out first, and White keeps its choices open.

steps.text: In the Bishop's Opening the bishop comes out before the knights. It aims at f7 at once, and White keeps its plans open.
Push the pawn in front of your king two squares. It takes space in the center and frees your queen and a bishop.

also.d2d4: Pushing the queen's pawn is also sound and leads to other openings. This lesson pushes the king's pawn.

steps.text: Bring the bishop out to c4. It aims at f7, which only the king guards.

also.g1f3: The knight move is the most common here, also sound, and leads to other openings. This lesson brings the bishop out first.
also.b1c3: That is the Vienna Game, also sound. This lesson brings the bishop out.

steps.after: This is the Berlin Defense, Black's most common answer: the knight attacks your pawn on e4.

steps.text: Guard the pawn with the pawn in front of your queen.

also.b1c3: That guards it too, also sound. This lesson uses the pawn.
also.d2d4: Giving the pawn for quick play is also sound. This lesson guards it.

steps.after: Black gets ready to push its queen pawn to d5 and chase your bishop.

steps.text: Bring the knight out. It attacks the pawn on e5.
Step the bishop back to b3. It stays on the line to f7.

wrong.f3e5: The pawn takes your bishop on c4, and you have only a pawn for it.

also.e4d5: Taking is also played. This lesson keeps the bishop.

steps.text: Bring the other knight out. It adds a guard to your pawn on e4.
steps.after: Black takes the pawn on e4 anyway.

steps.text: Do not take back yet. Jump the knight to g5: with the bishop it hits f7, and it attacks the pawn on e4 again.

also.c3e4: Taking back at once is also sound. This lesson goes to g5 first.

steps.text: Now take the pawn on e4 with the knight from c3.

also.g5e4: The other knight can take too, also sound. This lesson takes with this one.

steps.text: Take back with your other knight. Material is level.
steps.after: Your bishop on b3 keeps aiming at the black king for a long time.

summary: The bishop out first aims at the weak pawn by the king. White guards the center pawn and develops calmly.
